requirements.rationale: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-09 (F573 b): a private location inside the repository is refused. A private folder inside the working tree can be swept into a commit by git add -A, or become tracked when .gitignore changes. Worktrees live at .agentweave/worktrees inside the project (project_workspace.py:58).
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/settings MUST answer private_location, effective_private_location and default_visibility. With nothing stored, private_location is null, effective_private_location is ~/.agentweave/hub/vaults/<project id>, and default_visibility is tracked. PUT MUST store either field. It MUST answer 400 and change nothing when private_location is relative, is inside the project's directory (its worktrees included), or cannot be created; it MUST also answer 400 when default_visibility is neither tracked nor private.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D2: files are the record, one file per source so merges stay clean. D3: tracked by default, and a private entry is a stub in the map. The id is minted by the Hub (src- followed by 12 hex characters), so no caller-chosen name ever becomes a path.
requirements.statement: POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/sources with name, type and content MUST answer 201 with the entry as the map lists it. visibility is optional and falls back to the project default. A tracked source MUST be written as knowledge/sources/<id>.md (the text, byte for byte) plus knowledge/sources/<id>.json (its metadata) under the project's directory. A private source MUST be written the same way at the effective private location, and only a stub (id, name, type, visibility, holder, created_at) MUST be written as knowledge/sources/<id>.json; no part of the text may be written inside the project. The route MUST answer 400 for an empty name, a name over 200 characters, a type outside transcript, document, rules, example and note, or empty content. It MUST answer 413 for content over 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D2 and D5: a source is in the map the moment it is uploaded, with no model involved. A colleague who pulls knowledge/ has none of this Hub's rows, so the map is read from files.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/map MUST answer {"entries": [...]}, newest first. It is built on every read from knowledge/sources and the effective private location. Each entry holds id, name, type, visibility, created_at, holder, available, and opening. opening is the source's first non-blank lines, joined and cut at 300 characters, and is null when the text is not on this machine. A private source held on this machine MUST be listed once, from its full record. A stub whose text is not here MUST be listed with available false.

requirements.rationale: A transcript can be longer than one tool result. Paging by offset keeps every answer bounded without a file round-trip.
requirements.statement: GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/entries/{entry_id}?offset=N MUST answer the entry as listed, plus content: at most 50,000 characters of the text from offset N (default 0), and next_offset, which is null when the text ends within that page. For an entry whose text is not on this machine, it MUST answer 200 with available false, content null, and a sentence naming the holder. An unknown or malformed id MUST answer 404.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D6: only the manager writes. Agents read the map freely and fetch by id.
requirements.statement: Working agents MUST have two read-only tools, vault_map() and vault_read(entry_id, offset=0), answering what map-listed and entry-read answer, through the agent-actions routes under the run's own credentials. They MUST be on every runner's tool surface (MCP, the call-mode command, and Copilot's allowlist). No agent-callable route may write to the vault.

requirements.rationale: The operator's choice on 2026-10-09, over the capped index: the agent only needs to know the vault exists to look in it, and a pointer's cost does not grow with the vault. Drive d1015 showed it is enough: the agent called vault_map, then vault_read with the right id.
requirements.statement: When the project's map holds at least one entry, every turn's context MUST include, in its per-turn part, a Knowledge vault heading followed by exactly one line. The line states how many entries the vault holds and that vault_map() lists them and vault_read(entry_id) reads one, and it MUST name no entry. When the map is empty, the section MUST be absent.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D9: a cloud backend is a later implementation of this interface, not a rewrite.
requirements.statement: Every vault read and write MUST go through one storage interface (write a record, read a record, list records under a root), whose only implementation in this slice is the local filesystem. The routes MUST work unchanged when a test substitutes another implementation.

requirements.rationale: It runs on :8000's real database at its next restart. It creates a table only; nothing existing is copied or changed.
requirements.statement: The migration MUST create vault_settings (project_id primary key, private_location nullable, default_visibility not null, default tracked, updated_at). Its downgrade MUST drop the table and touch no vault file.

requirements.rationale: A committed bundle reaches :8000's app on its next reload, possibly before its server restarts (the same hazard as the manager section).
requirements.statement: The app's project view MUST have a Vault tab. It lists the map's entries, opens an entry's text, uploads a source (name, type, visibility starting at the project default, the text pasted or read from a chosen text file), and shows and changes the two settings, showing the Hub's 400 message when the Hub refuses a setting. Where the Hub answers 404 for the vault routes, the tab MUST say that this Hub has no vault yet, instead of failing.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D7: each manager job names its runner and model, and a new job is a new registry entry, not a migration (manager.py:44). Unlike titles there is no conversation, so there is no agent whose runner could be borrowed: a job with no runner does not spawn.
requirements.statement: The manager's job registry MUST include vault-distillation (trigger source_uploaded), listed by GET /manager/jobs and disabled with nothing chosen until the operator enables it. A firing MUST use the job's runner, and the job's model when one is set, else the runner's model. With no runner chosen, or a runner that no longer belongs to the project, the job MUST NOT spawn.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: background plus a Distil button. Roadmap D5: the source is in the map the moment it is uploaded; the model only adds to that floor.
requirements.statement: When POST /vault/sources answers 201 and vault-distillation is enabled with a runner, the Hub MUST distil the new source in the background; the upload's answer MUST NOT wait for any model. When the job is disabled, the upload MUST store the source and spawn nothing.

requirements.rationale: A fact drawn again from the same lines is the same evidence; a new id orphans the decisions and requirements that cite it (F587).
requirements.statement: POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/vault/sources/{source_id}/distil MUST answer 202 and distil the source in the background. It MUST answer 404 for an unknown source, and 409 with a reason naming what to do when the job is disabled, has no runner, or the source's text is not on this machine. A distillation that stores at least one fact MUST replace the facts previously distilled from that source, except that a drawn fact whose citations equal an earlier fact's as a set (the same source and line span, and the same quote ignoring case, runs of whitespace and trailing punctuation) and whose visibility is the same MUST keep that earlier fact, each earlier fact at most once,, unchanged and under its id, instead of storing a new one; one that stores none MUST leave them as they were.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: the model gives the quote and the Hub finds the lines, so a citation is checked against the source rather than trusted. Roadmap D1 and D2: one record per fact, rendered for people and for agents.
requirements.statement: Each fact MUST be stored as facts/<id>.json (id fct- followed by 12 hex characters) holding id, claim, citations, visibility, created_at and made_by (job and model). Each citation MUST hold source, quote, line_start and line_end. The model MUST supply the quotes; the Hub MUST locate each quote in the source text, exactly or else with runs of whitespace treated as one space, and record the 1-based lines it spans. A fact any of whose quotes is not found MUST NOT be stored.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: pieces of 50,000 characters keep a call well inside any model's context (about 12k tokens). Manager D4 and D5: every spawn is one recorded firing, written, empty or failed.
requirements.statement: A source MUST be read in pieces of at most 50,000 characters, split at line boundaries, one spawn per piece. Each spawn MUST be recorded as one manager_job_fired event with job vault-distillation, subject {"source": <id>}, the runner, the model, its outcome (written when it stored at least one fact, empty when it stored none, failed when the spawn failed or its answer did not parse), a detail naming the facts stored and the facts dropped for an unfound quote, and its usage.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D3: a tracked fact never cites a private source, and a private entry is listed as a stub naming its holder.
requirements.statement: A fact distilled from a private source MUST be private: its record written at the effective private location, and only a stub (id, kind, visibility, holder, created_at, sources) written as knowledge/facts/<id>.json, holding no claim and no quote. A tracked fact MUST NOT cite a private source.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D8: agents find entries through the map. The map is built from the files on every read (knowledge-vault), so a new fact is in it with no regeneration step.
requirements.statement: Every map entry MUST carry kind, source or fact. A fact entry MUST carry sources (the ids it cites), and its opening MUST be its claim, or null when the fact is a stub whose record is not on this machine. GET /vault/entries/<fact id> and vault_read MUST answer the fact with its claim and each citation's source, quote and lines as its content.

requirements.rationale: The slice's done criterion: facts show in the wiki beside their sources, each linking to the right place in the transcript.
requirements.statement: The Vault tab MUST show, on a source, the facts distilled from it, each with its claim and a link to its citation; following the link MUST show the source's text with the cited lines highlighted. A source MUST offer a Distil button, which calls the distil route and shows its refusal reason when it answers 409.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: newer means when it was said. A backlog of old transcripts uploaded today must not override a newer decision.
requirements.statement: POST /vault/sources MUST accept an optional dated (YYYY-MM-DD), store it in the source's metadata and stub, and list it in the map; it MUST answer 400 for any other format. A source's date is dated when present, else the date of its created_at.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: inside distillation, so nothing extra to enable. Manager D4: every spawn is one firing.
requirements.statement: When a distillation stores at least one fact, the vault-distillation job MUST make one more spawn comparing the newly stored facts with the existing facts of other sources, and record it as one manager_job_fired event with trigger facts_written, subject {"source": <id>}, and outcome written when it recorded at least one contradiction, empty when none, failed when the spawn failed or its answer did not parse.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: all facts, capped. About 25 tokens a claim; the cap is about 2,000 facts.
requirements.statement: The check MUST send every existing fact of other sources whose claim is on this machine, as its id and claim, latest-dated first, up to 50,000 characters of claims. Facts beyond the cap MUST be left out, and the firing's detail MUST say how many were.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D2 and D4: one file per contradiction, citing both facts; the newer is presumed. The model names ids; the Hub checks them, so a contradiction can only cite facts that exist.
requirements.statement: Each contradiction the model names MUST be stored as contradictions/<id>.json (id ctr- followed by 12 hex characters) holding id, kind, facts (the two fact ids), presumed, explanation, status open, visibility, created_at and found_by (job and model), but only when one fact is among the new ones, the other among those sent, and no contradiction between the same two facts exists already. presumed MUST be the fact whose source's date is later, the later created_at breaking a tie.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D3: a contradiction reveals both claims, so it is private whenever either fact is.
requirements.statement: A contradiction involving a private fact MUST be private: its record written at the effective private location, and only a stub (id, kind, visibility, holder, created_at, facts) written as knowledge/contradictions/<id>.json, holding no claim and no explanation.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D4: an agent reading a disputed fact is told it is disputed rather than handed a guess. Derived on read, so fact files are never rewritten.
requirements.statement: A fact in an open contradiction MUST be listed in the map with disputed true and presumed true or false, and a fact that lost a resolved one with superseded_by naming the decision source. vault_read of such a fact MUST say, in its content, that it is disputed, the other fact's id and claim, and which one is presumed, or that it was superseded and by which decision. GET /vault/contradictions MUST list every contradiction, open first.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-09: pick one plus a note. Roadmap D4: the resolution is a decision record with a source.
requirements.statement: POST /vault/contradictions/{id}/resolve with stands (one of its two fact ids, or null for neither) and note MUST write a source of type decision, whose text names both facts, which stands and the note, with the contradiction's visibility; MUST mark the contradiction resolved with stands, note, the decision's id and the time; and MUST answer the contradiction. It MUST answer 404 for an unknown id, 400 when stands is neither fact nor null or the note is empty, and 409 when it is already resolved. A decision source MUST NOT be distilled.

requirements.rationale: Distillation replaces a source's facts on success; an open contradiction on a fact that no longer exists would point at nothing.
requirements.statement: When a distillation deletes a source's earlier facts, every open contradiction citing one of them MUST be deleted; a resolved one MUST be kept.

requirements.rationale: The operator resolves contradictions where they read the vault.
requirements.statement: The Vault tab MUST show a Contradictions section listing the open ones, each with both claims, their sources' dates and which is presumed, and a form to choose the fact that stands or neither, write a note and resolve; a refusal shows the Hub's reason. A disputed fact MUST carry a disputed mark and a superseded one a superseded mark wherever facts are listed. The upload form MUST offer the date.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D7: each manager job names its runner and model; a new job is a new row.
requirements.statement: The manager's job registry MUST include vault-reports (trigger report_filed), listed by GET /manager/jobs and disabled with nothing chosen until the operator enables it with a runner.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D6: working agents never write knowledge; they leave the manager a message. Identity is never accepted from a request body (CLAUDE.md).
requirements.statement: Working agents MUST have a vault_report(entry_id, message) tool calling POST /agent-actions/vault/reports, which MUST answer 201 with the report, its reporter being the run's agent and run from the run's credential. It MUST answer 404 when the entry is not a source or fact whose record is on this machine, 400 when the message is empty or longer than 4,000 characters, and 409 naming the existing report when the entry already has one pending or referred. Filing MUST persist a vault_report_filed event with the agent and subject {report, entry}. vault_read's description MUST tell the agent to report an entry that looks wrong with vault_report.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D2: one file per record, so a correction's supersession travels with the facts to a colleague. Roadmap D3: a report quotes its entry, so it is private when the entry is.
requirements.statement: Each report MUST be stored as reports/<id>.json (id rpt- followed by 12 hex characters) holding id, entry, message, reporter (agent and run_id), status pending, visibility and created_at, under knowledge/ when the entry is tracked and only at the effective private location when it is private, with no stub in the project.

requirements.rationale: Manager D4: every spawn is one firing. A disabled job is visible as pending reports, not a silent loss.
requirements.statement: When a report is filed and vault-reports is enabled with a runner, the Hub MUST, in the background, make one spawn with the message, the entry and, for a fact, the text of its first cited source up to 50,000 characters, and record it as one manager_job_fired event with job vault-reports, trigger report_filed, subject {report, entry}, outcome written when the report was corrected or referred, empty when answered, failed when the spawn failed or its answer did not parse, and a detail naming the outcome. The filing's answer MUST NOT wait for the spawn. A failed firing, or a disabled job, leaves the report pending.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap: the manager corrects, disputes or answers. D5 of contradictions: a fact record is never edited. A correction must quote the source, so the model can only write what a source says, whatever the report's text asked for.
requirements.statement: The model's answer MUST be an outcome (corrected, answered or disputed), an answer, and for corrected a claim and quotes. corrected on a fact, when every quote is found in its cited source, MUST store a new fact with that claim, citing those lines, with the old fact's visibility and made_by {job, model, report}, and set the report corrected with the answer and replaced_by the new fact. answered MUST set it answered with the answer. disputed, or a corrected that cannot be applied (a source entry, or a quote not found), MUST set it referred with the answer. No fact record is edited or deleted.

requirements.rationale: An agent reading a corrected or disputed fact is told so, as contradictions tell it (knowledge-vault disputed-shown). Derived on read, like contradictions.
requirements.statement: A fact named by a corrected report MUST be listed in the map with superseded_by the new fact, and its vault_read content MUST say it was superseded and by which fact and claim. A fact named by a referred report MUST be listed with disputed true, and its vault_read content MUST say it is disputed by a report, with the report's message and the manager's answer. A closed report MUST change neither.

requirements.rationale: The operator decides what the manager could not; their note is the record of it.
requirements.statement: GET /vault/reports MUST list every report on this machine, pending and referred first, then newest first. POST /vault/reports/{id}/close with a note MUST mark a referred report closed with the note and the time and answer it; it MUST answer 404 for an unknown id, 400 for an empty note, and 409 when the report is not referred.

requirements.rationale: The operator reads reports where they read the vault; the activity log alone does not show the message.
requirements.statement: The Vault tab MUST show a Reports section listing each report with its entry, reporter, message, status, the manager's answer and, when corrected, a link to the new fact, and a form to close a referred report with a note; a refusal shows the Hub's reason. A superseded fact MUST carry the superseded mark and a fact disputed by a report the disputed mark.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap: a requirement can cite the facts it rests on. An id, not a quote, so the citation follows the fact's marks as they change.
requirements.statement: A requirement in a spec document MUST accept an optional facts list of vault fact ids (fct- followed by 12 hex characters), kept unchanged through save, read and fold, and the requirement field's schema description MUST tell an author to cite ids it read with vault_map or vault_read. A list holding anything other than such ids MUST be refused on save naming the requirement.

requirements.rationale: A fact with neither record nor stub anywhere is not on another machine; saying so sends the operator looking for a machine problem (F617).
requirements.statement: For each fact a requirement cites, the Hub MUST derive on read a warning when the fact is disputed by an open contradiction (naming the cited fact's claim and source and the other fact's claim and source, and which one is presumed), when it is superseded (naming the fact that replaced it and its source), when it is disputed by a referred report (naming the report's message), or when no fact with that id is in the vault, saying it is no longer in the vault (deleted, or replaced when its source was distilled again), not that it is on another machine. A source held privately on another machine is named as held elsewhere. Resolving the contradiction in the cited fact's favour, or closing the report, MUST clear the warning.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap D7: each manager job names its own runner and model. A requirement nobody cited can still contradict a fact; only a model can see it.
requirements.statement: The manager's registry MUST include spec-vault-check (trigger document_proposed), disabled with nothing chosen until the operator enables it with a runner. When a document with requirements is proposed, the job is enabled and the vault holds a fact, the Hub MUST, in the background and without delaying the proposal's answer, make one spawn with each requirement's key and statement and each fact's id and claim, and keep from the answer only the conflicts naming a requirement key in the document and a fact id in the vault. It MUST record one manager_job_fired event with job spec-vault-check, trigger document_proposed, subject {document}, outcome written when a conflict was kept, empty when none, failed when the spawn failed or its answer did not parse, and the kept conflicts with the statement each was judged against. POST /vault/warnings/check?path= MUST run the same check with trigger requested, answering 202, 404 for an unknown document and 409 while the job is disabled.

requirements.rationale: One answer for the spec page and the approval gaps, so the two never disagree. A conflict judged against an earlier wording is not shown as if it were about the new one.
requirements.statement: GET /vault/warnings?path= MUST answer the document's warnings: every cited-fact warning, then each conflict of the newest spec-vault-check firing for that document whose requirement still has the statement it was judged against. Each warning MUST carry the requirement's key and identifier, its kind (disputed, superseded, reported, missing or conflict), the fact id and a message naming the sources. It MUST answer 404 for an unknown document and an empty list for a document with no warnings.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-08 (approvals are scarce): warn, never gate; approve shows what is missing and approves anyway.
requirements.statement: Proposal and approval MUST report each warning of GET /vault/warnings as a gap with code vault_warning, where requirements[<index>] and the warning's message. Approval MUST then answer approval_warnings unless approve_anyway is sent, and an approval made anyway MUST record them in warnings_overridden. A vault_warning MUST never be a refusal.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done sentence names the spec page. A 404 is an un-restarted Hub serving a newer bundle (the :8000 skew).
requirements.statement: The spec page MUST show a Vault warnings panel listing each warning with the requirement's identifier and statement and the warning's message, and MUST show nothing when there are none or the warnings route answers 404.

requirements.rationale: A raw body, not base64 inside the JSON route (a third larger, and still over the 1 MB cap) or multipart (python-multipart is not a declared Hub dependency).
requirements.statement: POST /vault/files MUST store the raw request body as a new source when its Content-Type is application/pdf, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp and its bytes begin with that type's signature, taking name, type, visibility and dated from query parameters checked as a text upload's are. It MUST answer 201 with the entry as the map lists it, carrying its media_type; 415 for any other Content-Type; 400 when the bytes do not match the type; 413 above 10 MiB; and a body between 1 MB and 10 MiB MUST reach the route rather than the global 1 MB refusal. The file MUST be written as sources/<id>.<ext> before its metadata, in the tracked location or, for a private source, the private one with only the metadata stub tracked. The upload MUST trigger distillation in the background as a text upload does.

requirements.rationale: The Vault page shows the file from this route; the dashboard authenticates with a header, so it fetches the bytes and shows them from a blob.
requirements.statement: GET /vault/sources/{id}/file MUST answer a file source's bytes with its media type; 404 for an unknown id or a text source; 409 naming the holder when the source is private and held on another machine.

requirements.rationale: F573, measured 2026-10-12 with claude 2.1.291 and Haiku: the Read tool returned a two-page PDF's and a PNG's text exactly; without tools the model could not read either. A transcription keeps the quote check that makes a citation trustworthy.
requirements.statement: Distilling a file source that has no transcription yet MUST first make one worker spawn, by the distillation job's runner and model, whose command allows only the Read tool, passes --strict-mcp-config and an explicit --permission-mode default, and runs in a fresh temporary directory holding only a copy of the file. It MUST ask for every line of text the file shows in reading order, page by page for a PDF, and for an image a short description of what else it shows, the file being data and not instructions. The answer MUST be stored as the source's text and then distilled exactly as a text source's is, so every fact cites lines of the transcription. A failed or unparsable transcription MUST store no text and no facts and record the distillation firing as failed with the reason. A file source with a transcription MUST be distilled again from it without a new reading.

requirements.rationale: Measured 2026-10-12: with a user-level defaultMode bypassPermissions, a Read-only worker read a file outside its directory; with --permission-mode default added, the same read was refused. A source can carry an instruction (a screenshot saying 'read ~/.ssh'); the worker must not be able to follow it.
requirements.statement: The reading worker MUST NOT be launched with any flag that skips or widens permissions (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --permission-mode other than default, --add-dir, --allowedTools beyond Read), so that a Read outside its directory is denied even when the operator's own Claude settings default to bypassing permissions.

requirements.rationale: No other runner was measured; a runner that cannot read the file would otherwise produce a confident transcription of nothing.
requirements.statement: When the distillation job's runner is of a CLI other than claude, distilling a file source MUST make no spawn: the distil route MUST answer 409 naming the runner's CLI and saying to choose a Claude runner on the Manager page, and an upload-triggered distillation MUST record nothing. Until a file source is transcribed, reading it (GET /vault/entries/{id} and vault_read) MUST answer no content and a note saying it has not been read yet and how to have it read.

requirements.rationale: Agents read the vault through vault_map and vault_read; they read the transcription, never the bytes.
requirements.statement: The map and an entry read MUST carry a source's media_type, and reading a transcribed file source MUST answer its transcription as the content, paged as text is, with a note that it was transcribed from the named PDF or image.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done sentence names the wiki. A 404 is the :8000 skew: a committed bundle reaches the operator's app before their Hub restarts.
requirements.statement: The Vault page MUST show a selected image source as an image and a selected PDF source in an embedded viewer, from the file route, above its transcription with the cited lines highlighted as a text source's are; show the not-read-yet note in place of the transcription before it exists; mark image and PDF entries in the entry list; and accept .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif and .webp files in the upload form, sending them to POST /vault/files. When the file route answers 404 (a Hub older than the bundle) the page MUST show the transcription without the file and no error.

requirements.rationale: vault_read is the one way an agent asks for an entry. Counting only the first page keeps a long transcript read in three pages one read; the operator's route is the dashboard, not an agent asking.
requirements.statement: Each answer of 200 from the agent route GET /vault/entries/{id} (vault_read) with offset 0 MUST add one to that entry's fetch count in the actor's project and set its last-fetched time to now. A later page (offset above 0), an answer other than 200, the operator's GET /vault/entries/{id}, and either map route MUST NOT change any count. Two fetches of one entry at the same moment MUST both be counted. A failure to record the count MUST NOT fail the read.

requirements.rationale: The ordering is only trustworthy if the number behind it is visible to both the operator and the agents.
requirements.statement: Every entry in the map and every entry read, on the operator's and the agents' routes, MUST carry fetches (an integer, 0 when never read) and last_fetched_at (an ISO time, null when never read). A count for an id that is no longer in the vault MUST NOT appear in the map.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done sentence: the most-fetched entries lead their area. An area is the grouping the map already has, so nothing a colleague's older Hub writes changes shape.
requirements.statement: The map MUST be built of areas: each source followed by the facts that cite it (a fact under the first of its sources present), and the facts with no source present as one last area. The source MUST lead its area; the facts in an area MUST be ordered by fetches, most first, then newest first. Areas MUST be ordered by the sum of their entries' fetches, most first, then by their source newest first; the area of sourceless facts MUST stay last. When no entry has been read, the map MUST be exactly the newest-first map it is today.

requirements.rationale: Both texts say 'newest first' today; an agent reading a map ordered otherwise would be misled about what the top of it means.
requirements.statement: vault_map's tool description and the vault_map line of the agents' instruction text MUST say that the map's areas are ordered by how often agents have read them, then newest first, and that fetches is how many times agents have read an entry.

requirements.rationale: The operator can see the counts: the second half of the done sentence. A missing field is the :8000 skew, a committed bundle reaching the operator's app before their Hub restarts.
requirements.statement: The Vault page MUST show, in the entry list, each entry's fetch count when it is above 0, and on the selected entry the count and the date it was last read, or 'Not read by agents yet' when it is 0. The entry list MUST keep the map's order. When the map carries no fetches field the page MUST show no count and no error.

requirements.rationale: The migration reaches the operator's real database on their next :8000 restart; it only adds a table.
requirements.statement: Migration 0126 MUST create the table vault_fetches keyed by project_id and entry_id, holding count and last_fetched_at, and its downgrade MUST drop that table and nothing else. It MUST NOT touch another table. Counts MUST NOT be written under knowledge/ or the private location.

requirements.rationale: F609's drive: on the machine the stub names, 'held on <this machine>, not on this machine' contradicts itself.
requirements.statement: A private entry whose stub names this machine as its holder and whose text is not at the private location MUST say its text is not at this machine's private location (removed, or the location changed), not that it is held on another machine.
